data.name: Kapila
data.long_meaning: The one who is dark in complexion, or the one who is filled with wisdom and knowledge.

in_sanskrit.name: कपिल
in_sanskrit.long_meaning: The name Kapila is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Kapi’, which means black, dark, or dark-skinned. In Hindu mythology, Kapila is the name of several important figures, including Kapila Muni, the sage who is considered the founder of Jainism.

in_hindi.name: कपिला
in_hindi.meaning: सूरज के पूजारी | सूरज के प्रसादी
in_hindi.long_meaning: In Hindi, the name Kapila can be translated to ‘the worshiper of the sun’ or ‘the one who receives the sun’s blessings’. The name is also associated with the Hindu deity Surya (the sun god) and is considered an auspicious name for a baby boy.

vedic_reference.note: The name Kapila is mentioned in various Hindu scriptures, including the Mahabharata and the Puranas. Kapila Muni is considered the 27th Tirthankara in Jainism and is revered by both Jains and Hindus.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kapila is rooted in ancient Indian history, originating from the Hindu scriptures. Kapila is mentioned as a sage and a master of Yoga in various religious texts such as the Puranas and the Mahabharata. In Hindu mythology, Kapila is also considered to be one of the ten primary avatars or aspects of Lord Shiva, known as Adi-Guru or the first teacher.
data.spiritual_significance: In spiritual terms, Kapila symbolizes knowledge, wisdom, and enlightenment. His name reflects his deep understanding and mastery of the spiritual path, and he is often revered as a model for seekers of truth and self-realization. The name Kapila can inspire us to seek knowledge and wisdom, and to strive towards spiritual growth and self-realization.
